input.question: Why does it take hours to install big programs and games but seconds to uninstall it?
input.ground_truth: When you are installing a game, you are writing the files to your hard drive. It has to remember where to access those files. The uninstallation is just forgetting those locations on your drive, not actually erasing them.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of building blocks (that’s like a big program or game on your computer). 

When you want to **install** the game, it’s like someone has to bring all the blocks from a faraway place and carefully put them in the right spots, one by one. That takes a long time because there are so many blocks!

But when you want to **uninstall** the game, it’s like you just pick up the whole box and put it away. The computer doesn’t have to move each block one by one—it just knows where the whole box is and can take it away quickly.

So, putting all the blocks in takes a long time (installing), but taking the whole box away is fast (uninstalling)!
